day.note: The vote is near and Finley and Ellis are leaning on me. I'll push suspicion onto Alex, whose Falcon story is the source of the pressure, and keep Casey out of it.

day.text: Blair, you dodged your role until late, and Casey denies the visit you claim. I'm throwing at you. Finley, Alex, please check your votes.
day.note: Blair dodged the role question and gave a claim Casey denies, so I still see Blair as the most likely Meowfia. I'll throw one low card at Blair and keep my high cards.

Alex.note: I'm Farm with the Falcon again. Blair leads the scores and their claims have been consistent, so I'll visit Blair to learn who they went to tonight.

Blair.note: I'm Meowfia with a Mouser and a Wink. I'll visit Casey to learn their role and look for a teammate or a target.

Casey.note: As the Sphinx I learn the Farm roles in play: Eagle, Falcon, Kookaburra, Tit. I'll name Eagle and visit whoever holds it to learn their identity.

Drew.note: I'm Farm Eagle with no leads, so I'll visit Blair, who has been consistent so far, and learn their visitors.

Ellis.note: I'm Farm as the Tit this round. Blair leads the scores, so I'll check Blair and guess Owl, a role they've claimed before.

Finley.note: As Kookaburra I want to learn a role. I'll visit Drew, who hasn't been under suspicion, to get information.

events.text: Blair was visited by: Ellis, Alex.

audit: Drew lays 2 eggs in Drew's nest

Alex.feeling: Messy and tense: Blair and Casey contradict each other over the visit, Drew is dead, and the vote is splitting toward Blair.

Blair.feeling: I'm Meowfia with Casey as my Sphinx partner, so I'm stuck defending a claim that doesn't fit and the table is closing in on me.

Casey.feeling: Tense and murky: Blair's Owl claim contradicts what I know, but I'm the one holding back a vote while the table pushes toward throwing at Blair.

Drew.feeling: Tense and muddled: Blair dodged the role question, Casey denies a visit Alex and Blair both describe, and I'm dead, so I can't steer the vote.

Ellis.feeling: Messy and contradictory: the visit claims conflict, and Blair's dodging makes it hard to trust anyone.

Finley.feeling: Round 3 is tangled: Alex, Blair, Casey, and Ellis all contradict each other about who visited Blair and Casey, and I can't tell who is lying.

Alex.note: Ellis and Finley are committed to Blair, and Blair's Owl story is the one I'd still question. I'll join the majority with my zero-value wild W8 so I don't spend real eggs.

Blair.note: I'm Meowfia, and Casey is my teammate. Ellis is the Farm voice pushing hardest on me, so I'll throw at Ellis and keep my two highest cards.

Casey.note: Blair claimed Owl, which isn't among the Farm roles in play, so Blair is Meowfia and so is my partner. I'll throw three cards at Ellis to draw votes away from Blair and push Ellis, a Farm player, toward elimination.

Drew.note: I'm dead, so my throw won't count as a vote and only matters for scoring. Throwing my Wild, which is worth 0 either way, costs nothing, and Alex's story is the one most likely to be false.

Ellis.note: I'm sticking with Blair as the target and throwing one low card, H2, to keep my higher cards.

Finley.note: Blair dodged the role question and Casey denies the visit Blair claims, so Blair is my suspect. I'll throw my Wild and a low 2 at Blair to add votes for the eggsecution.

Alex.confusing: The Sphinx's night choice was unclear: I named Hawk blindly, and the dawn report only identified the Hawk without hinting at other Meowfia. The Owl's rule about learning animals rather than players was also easy to misread.
Alex.fun: Round 2 was the most fun: my Falcon visit on Drew matched Blair's Owl and Finley's Tit, and the table converged on Ellis's shifting story.
Alex.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who visited whom, since the Owl and Falcon claims were hard to cross-check.
Alex.regret: In round 1 I claimed Owl and invented a visit to Drew that everyone rejected, so I should have stayed vague. In round 3 I kept pressing Casey over Blair's visit when Blair was the actual Mouser, so I should have pushed Blair's role harder earlier.

Blair.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion and the Owl's visitor report were hard to weigh, since a confused player's dawn report can be wrong without them knowing which parts. Also, nest counts were hard to read because the day listing shows changes, not totals.
Blair.fun: Round 3, when I was secretly Meowfia and had to explain my Mouser visit and an Owl claim while Casey, my teammate, denied the visit, and the table nearly voted me out. Watching Ellis's story wobble and then fall apart in Round 2 was also satisfying.
Blair.change: I would make the dawn reports clearer about who is confused, so players can tell which parts of a claim to trust. I would also make it clear which player's secret role is hidden from teammates.
Blair.regret: In Round 3 I should have claimed a role that didn't contradict Casey's visit, and I should not have used my Wink on Drew, the strongest Farm claimant, since it left the table nothing to check. I would instead have stayed quiet and let the Farm players argue among themselves.

Casey.confusing: Dawn reports were hard to trust: Drew's Kookaburra confusion and Ellis's changing story made it unclear whose egg counts and visits were real. I also couldn't tell which Farm roles were actually in play to test Blair's claim.
Casey.fun: Round 2's day, where Ellis's Pigeon story fell apart against Finley's unchanged nest, and the table turned on them within a single day. It was a clean case of cross-checking egg counts against claims.
Casey.change: I'd make the dawn reports clearer about confusion, so players can tell when an egg count or visit claim is unreliable.
Casey.regret: In Round 2, as Floofer on the Meowfia side, I threw three cards at Ellis, who was my own Meowfia partner, which helped hand the round to Farm. Instead I should have thrown at a Farm player and kept my partner safe.

Drew.confusing: The Kookaburra's confusion rule was hard to track, since my dawn report sometimes said I was confused and I couldn't tell whether my visit results were wrong. Also, Alex's Falcon and Owl claims in round 1 were never checked against the true roles.
Drew.fun: Round 1's Owl-versus-Kookaburra standoff, where the table caught Alex's story by cross-checking nest changes, was a satisfying read. Calling the CAW vote and seeing Alex eggsecuted as Meowfia confirmed the reasoning.
Drew.change: I'd make the Storyteller reveal each player's confusion status or visit results more clearly, so Farm players can separate a wrong report from a lying one.
Drew.regret: In round 3 I backed the Alex-Falcon and Blair-Owl chain too quickly and didn't press Blair's late role claim before my throw. Knowing Blair was the Mouser, I would have pushed harder on Blair's role dodge in beat 2 and called for the vote on Blair earlier.

Ellis.confusing: The Kookaburra and Owl reports were hard to trust, since confused players get wrong egg counts and the table had no way to tell who was confused. Nobody could easily tell which Falcon or Eagle claims were real.
Ellis.fun: Round 1 went cleanly: the table caught Alex's false Owl story and voted them out. Watching the Farm side converge on a single liar felt satisfying.
Ellis.change: I would make the dawn egg reports and confusion notices clearer, so players can check each other's claims without guessing which reports were wrong.
Ellis.regret: As the Mouser in round 2, I invented a Pigeon claim that my own egg count contradicted, which got me eggsecuted. I should have stayed quiet or claimed a role that fit my zero-change nest.

Finley.confusing: The Tit and Kookaburra rules were hard to track, especially whether a Kookaburra visit made the visitor's report unreliable. How Dead players still throw, and how the consolation card returns, were unclear at first.
Finley.fun: Round 1 was satisfying: Alex's Owl story fell apart under cross-checking, and the table converged on the right Meowfia.
Finley.change: I would have dawn reports say which visitor gave each egg, so public claims about egg gains are easier to verify.
Finley.regret: In Round 3 I trusted Alex's Falcon claim and pushed Blair without questioning Casey harder. Casey was the Sphinx and was lying about the visit, so I should have pressed Casey's denial earlier.

review.title: Wink Wins Round Three
review.headline: Meowfia lost two rounds, then a Wink and a lie stole the game.
review.summary: Round 1 was a lone Sphinx with a bad Owl bluff, and the table piled on Alex fast. In round 2 the two Meowfia did not know each other. Ellis's Wink killed an accuser but could not save him, and Ellis was eggsecuted. In round 3 Blair's Wink on the Eagle and Casey's heavy throws got a Farm player eggsecuted. Both Meowfia finished first and second, because that one round banked huge cards.

rounds.recap: Alex was the lone Meowfia Sphinx. He claimed Owl and invented a visit by Ellis to Drew, and Drew and Ellis both contradicted it. The table agreed within a beat, and Alex was eggsecuted. Everyone else won small.

Casey (Floofer) and Ellis (Mouser) were Meowfia. Ellis dodged giving a role, then claimed Pigeon. Finley's report showed no egg, which exposed the claim. Ellis winked Finley, but the table still threw at Ellis. Farm won.

Blair (Mouser) and Casey (Sphinx) were Meowfia. Blair winked Drew, the Eagle. Blair's Owl claim collided with Casey's Hawk claim, and Casey denied a visit that Alex's Falcon read confirmed. Farm split between Blair and Casey. Casey's heavy throws at Ellis and Blair's two at Ellis got a Farm player eggsecuted. Meowfia won big.

highlights.text: Alex invented an Owl read blaming Ellis, and Ellis and Drew each knocked it down in one line.
Ellis claimed Pigeon, and Finley caught it because his own nest had no egg. Ellis then winked Finley mid-day.
Blair winked the Eagle, Drew, who was the best-supported Farm voice.
Casey denied that Blair visited him, which was true for Casey's own report but not for Alex's Falcon read. Farm split, and a Farm player took the eggsecution.

confusions.what: Claimed Owl and invented a visit and a visitor, although a Sphinx's night showed him no such information. He then said he might have been confused, which is not a role effect that applies.

Said Blair's Owl claim could not be true because Owl is not among Farm roles in play. He also denied that Blair visited him, although visits are not known to a Sphinx or Hawk. This revealed knowledge he should have hidden.
Treated Finley's +0 nest as proof that Ellis's Pigeon claim was false without considering that Ellis could have been hugged or that nest size already counts the deal.
Said his visit to Finley gave no egg change, then claimed Pigeon, which contradicts that. This was a contradiction made under pressure rather than a rules misread.

Said Alex's Owl visit did not fit because he had no egg change, but an Owl only lays an egg if nobody else visited Drew. He had no visitors but Casey's, so the contradiction was less clear than he said.

worked: The Wink created sharp moments. Ellis's round-2 Wink on Finley and Blair's round-3 Wink on Drew both silenced a key voice mid-day with no one knowing who did it.
Cross-checking egg counts against claims. Finley's +0 nest versus Ellis's Pigeon claim was a clean, fair catch.
Meowfia not knowing each other. Blair and Casey's mismatched Owl and Hawk claims in round 3 caused real trouble for both of them.
Throw sizes as signals and score. Casey's big round-3 throw banked a huge score and decided first and second place.
problems: Round 1 was a quick pile-on. A lone Meowfia with a bad bluff gets killed by beat 3. Fix: give the lone Meowfia more cover or role information.
The winning team's banked cards swing the whole game. Round 3 gave Blair 13 and Casey 17 and ended the contest. Fix: cap banked points or reduce how much high cards matter.
Dead Farm players like Drew and Finley lose all voice, and the Wink has no real counter. Fix: give Farm some way to detect or answer winks.
Early rounds are mostly random visits with no information. Players mostly said the same things and then said nothing. Fix: reward unique information or give them a reason to commit to a target.
Players dodged the role question for several beats (Ellis, Blair) and the table could not act on it. Fix: make refusing to claim costly, or have the app prompt the claim.
